title: Soon, you won't pick your AI. The app will.
subtitle: ChatGPT and Claude now offer dozens of models. My bet is the menu disappears, and the choosing moves behind the counter. Here's what that does to money, to getting the job done, and to power.

youtube_description:
Open Claude or ChatGPT and there's a menu of models. My bet: soon you won't see any of them. The app will pick for you.

OpenAI already tried. GPT-5 launched with a router that picked for you, and on day one Sam Altman said it "seemed way dumber". People complain about too much choice, then riot when it's taken away. I think the menu goes anyway. Here's what that does to what you pay, to the answers you get, and to who holds the power. | 3 minute watch

My prediction: by the end of 2027, the big AI apps won't show you a list of models unless you ask.

linkedin_post:
If your product runs on someone else's AI, watch the model menu.

Today ChatGPT and Claude let you pick the model. My bet is that choice moves behind the counter: the app picks for you, and you only get a choice if you go looking. OpenAI already tried it with GPT-5's router.

When the app picks, your costs and your quality can move without you touching anything. So stop asking "which AI is best?" and ask "what does a good answer cost me, all in?" Pin the exact version you run on. Rerun the same test every month. If the results move and you didn't change anything, now you know who did.

My prediction: by the end of 2027, the big AI apps won't show you a list of models unless you ask.
